quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: Lilly's triple agonist, retatrutide, delivered substantial (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Lilly reported detailed results of the Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial of retatrutide, its investigational once-weekly GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist, in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight (presented at EASD and published in The Lancet). At 80 weeks (efficacy estimand), from an average baseline of 106.4 kg, retatrutide 4 mg, 9 mg and 12 mg cut body weight by 12.7%, 19.1% and 20.8% versus 4.0% on placebo; participants with a baseline BMI of 35 or higher on 12 mg lost 23.4%, and 59.5% on 12 mg no longer met the BMI criteria for obesity. A1C fell by 1.4%, 1.6% and 1.5% (placebo 0.2%) from an average baseline of 7.7%, with up to 40.0% reaching an A1C of <5.7% (not controlled for type 1 error); 52.0% on 12 mg reached at least 20% weight reduction. The highest dose reduced triglycerides by 39.5%, non-HDL cholesterol by 19.6%, systolic blood pressure by 10.8 mmHg and hsCRP by 58.3%. The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal, and discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.8% (4 mg), 11.6% (9 mg) and 7.7% (12 mg) versus 4.9% on placebo.
